title: Annotatio IV §.VI close: Irenaeus Lib. 5 — nourished by creature, not natural body; stop before §.VII
pass_a_gloss: For so again Irenæus proceeds in Book 5 against Heresies ch. 12: As a grain of wheat, falling into the earth and dissolved, rises manifold, and receiving the word of God becomes Eucharist (which is the body and blood of Christ); so also our bodies, namely of the faithful, nourished from it and laid in the earth and dissolved, shall rise (namely with joy) in their time. Nay, lest anyone imagine the most holy Father thinks our bodies are nourished by Christ’s body rather than by Eucharistic bread severed from every common use, he adds a little later: We are nourished by the Creature, and He Himself supplies us the Creature; Since He confirmed the Cup, which is a creature, as His blood, and that bread, which is a creature, as His Body. When therefore the Cup and bread receive the word of God, there is made the Eucharist of the blood and body of Christ (not the blood and body of Christ themselves) from which (cup and bread) the substance of our flesh is increased and consists. Seeing it would be said not without great absurdity and impiety that our bodies are increased and consist from Christ’s natural body and blood; since nothing can naturally increase our body except what is converted by alteration into our flesh and blood, which it is blasphemous to affirm of Christ’s incorruptible body.
pass_b_english: Irenaeus Adv. Haer. 5.12: as wheat falls, dissolves, and rises manifold into Eucharist (body and blood of Christ), so faithful bodies nourished from it shall rise. We are nourished by the Creature He supplies — cup and bread as creature confirmed as His blood and Body.

When cup and bread receive God’s word there is made the Eucharist of His blood and body — not the blood and body themselves — from which our flesh’s substance increases. To say our bodies grow from Christ’s natural incorruptible body would be absurd and blasphemous.
source_text: Ita enim iterum Irenæus Lib. 5. contra Hæret. cap. 12. pergit: Quemadmodum granum tritici, decidens in terram & dissolutum, multiplex surgit, & percipiens verbum Dei fit Eucharistia; (quod est corpus & sanguis Christi); Sic & nostra, scil. fidelium, corpora, ex eo nutrita, & reposita in terram ac resoluta, resurgent (scil. cum gaudio) in suo tempore. Quin, ne quis sibi imaginetur, sanctissimum Patrem opinari, corpora nostra corpore Christi nutriri, non verò pane Eucharistico potius ab omni usu communi sejuncto, addit paulò post: Per Creaturam nutrimur, Creaturam autem ipse nobis præstat; Cùm Calicem, qui est creatura, suum sanguinem, & eum panem, qui est creatura, suum Corpus confirmavit. Quando ergo Calix & panis percipiunt verbum Dei, fit Eucharistia sanguinis & corporis Christi (non ipse sanguis & corpus Christi) ex quibus (calice scil. & pane) augetur & consistit carnis nostræ substantia. Quandoquidem non sine magna absurditate impietateque diceretur, ex naturali Christi corpore & sanguine, nostra corpora augeri ac consistere; cùm nihil corpus nostrum naturaliter augere possit, nisi quod per alterationem in carnem nostram & sanguinem convertitur, quod de corpore Christi incorruptibili affirmare blasphemum est.
